highlights.title: Apple ‘Pro and Tell’ event: everything announced this week
highlights.summary: Apple closed out its week of product announcements with a "Pro and Tell" event on Wednesday, where it took the wraps off its long-rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro. Though Apple may have saved its biggest and most exciting update for last, it revealed a few other device upgrades and updates in the…
body: Along with a new touchscreen MacBook Pro, Apple also took the wraps off an OLED iPad Mini and M6-upgraded Macs this week.

Apple CEO John Ternus revealed the company’s first MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, allowing you to perform gestures on your screen like scrolling, swiping, and pinching. The company says the touch sensor is “built directly into the display panel,” not on top of it, which helps to reduce latency.

The device also offers a tandem OLED display, a 120Hz refresh rate, and 2,000 nits of brightness. It’s also lighter than previous MacBook Pro models, with the 14-inch model weighing three pounds. The device brings back the illuminated Apple logo on its lid as well, and is the first to come with a Dynamic Island for viewing real-time updates, searching for files, and using Siri AI.

The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display starts at $2,899 with a 14-inch display and M5 Pro chip, while the 16-inch version starts at $3,399 with an M5 Pro. There are also configurations available with an M5 Max chip. The touchscreen MacBook is available to preorder starting today, with availability starting November 6th.

It comes as the WRU wrestles with a financial crisis that saw it announce a loss of £18.1m for 2025-26 last week, a figure that it says strengthens its case to reduce the number of regions from four to three.
The Prem is aiming to expand from 10 to 12 sides in time for the 2029-2030 season and English rugby’s governing bodies insist their priority is to back domestic teams.

“Resources are currently focused on supporting English clubs throughout the pyramid who aspire to join the league,” they said in a joint a statement. “The Prem is an attractive league and responsibility for its expansion sits with the Men’s Professional Rugby Board (MPRB), which has established detailed entry criteria that any prospective club would need to satisfy.”

highlights.title: Chrome’s enhanced autofill can now pull info from Gmail to help you fill out forms
highlights.summary: Following improvements made to Chrome's enhanced autofill last year that included your name, passport number, email address, and physical addresses sourced from your Google Accounts and services like Google Wallet, the feature is now expanding.
body: Using Gemini with Personal Intelligence, it can find details like order numbers, tracking, and travel bookings.

The expanded autofill capabilities can retrieve details such as a shipment’s tracking number, travel details like a flight booking number or hotel reservation, or the order number of a recent purchase. Sensitive data presented as a suggestion while completing a form remains encrypted, and users can manage what enhanced autofill has access to in Chrome’s settings, or turn it off completely.

Google is starting to roll out the enhanced autofill improvements today in the US. They’ll be available through Gemini in Chrome for users with Personal Intelligence turned on in the desktop, Android, and iOS versions of the browser.

highlights.title: Major 'Avatar: The Last Airbender' Game Finally Lives Up To The Hype
highlights.summary: With its fantastic animation and incredible attention to detail, Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game felt like it was destined for greatness. And perhaps the fighting game could have gone down as the best Avatar interactive experience ever made had it not been released in July 2026 without some key…
body: The game just received its fourth content update, and it's the biggest overhaul of the title yet. Avatar State Aang and Nightmare Korra, the powered-up forms of the series' protagonists, were redrawn from the ground up and now have new attacks and techniques. All the other characters have been rebalanced as well, though not quite to the same degree.

One of the biggest complaints players had around launch was Avatar Legends ' lack of a ranked mode, which made it difficult for newbie players to find their footing against expert players. The new patch fixes that issue with the addition of a ranked mode and a competitive ladder, as well as a brand-new spectator mode. Developer Gameplay Ground International is also promising beginner-friendly lobbies, new tutorials, and combo trials that break down advanced tactics. The idea is to help new players stick around for the long term — which is important when the game is about to launch on Switch 2 on October 29.

highlights.summary: LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse at its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years. As rumored, it includes an OLED display, and for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change that Apple has long debated the merits of.
body: Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging, and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom. It does not appear to be a 2-in-1 convertible design though; all the footage was of people reaching up to touch the screen in a normal laptop configuration.

The OLED display (which Apple is of course calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: it can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared. The display retains the 120Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.

Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences. First, it’s much lighter. Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.

highlights.title: Meta says it’ll probably delay its controversial new business terms again
highlights.summary: Meta says it may push the implementation of its new business terms past November 20th as it faces backlash from publishers over concerns about AI training. In a post on X, Meta communications head Andy Stone said the company does "not plan to make policy changes without a full consultation with…
body: The new business terms, which were supposed to take effect on October 30th, initially appeared to give Meta permission to train its AI models on the news sites that use Facebook and Instagram. Meta later changed its policies to remove language indicating that it could “train” its products on content scraped from these sites, but legal experts told Nieman Lab that the update still isn’t enough to rule out that possibility. Meta responded to these concerns by delaying the implementation of its terms until November 20th. Now, enforcement may be delayed indefinitely.

“We’ve heard publishers’ feedback on our proposed ads and business terms update,” Stone said. “We’re committed to getting this right, and as we expect this consultation could extend beyond November 20, in which case we’d delay implementation of the updated terms. Until then our existing terms remain in place.”

highlights.title: ‘This isn’t supposed to happen’: giant-slaying Fleetwood revels in fairytale Arsenal win
highlights.summary: Fishing town in disbelief the morning after its footballing minnows beat mighty Arsenal on penalties. On a wet and windy night on the north-west coast of England, a League Two side sensationally knocked the Premier League champions out of the Carabao Cup.
body: Arsenal played at their iconic Highbury stadium until 2006, and Fleetwood’s ground has the same title, being named after Highbury Avenue, the adjoining street.

Fleetwood also play in red shirts with white sleeves in the style of the classic Arsenal kit. Nobody is exactly sure why, but according to Ray Curtis, a barman in the town’s King’s Arms: “Fleetwood’s first ever kit, the home kit, was given to them by Arsenal.”
And in the 2000s, not long after Patrick Vieira captained Arsenal, Fleetwood boasted a namesake star: a Brazilian striker called Magno Vieira.

At the 5,300-capacity Highbury on Wednesday morning, the floodlights that Fleetwood had hired for the occasion were being packed away. “It’s back to reality, back to being a League Two team, that’s our normal,” said Zsofia Wright, the ticket office and retail manager.

highlights.title: Discord's Massive New Change Will Shake Up The Entire Internet
highlights.summary: The best and worst thing about Discord is that messages sent on its chat servers are ephemeral. On the one hand, it's nice to know that things said in a casual setting won't necessarily be plastered on the internet forever.
body: Discord recently announced that communities with at least 1,000 members will soon start to see their messages appear on public search engines like Google. Such communities will generate what Discord calls a Server Web Page, and these will showcase summaries of discussions happening on public channels. Discord's blog post states that some, but not all, of the content shared on those widely accessible channels will gradually start to populate on Google beginning in December 2026.

The platform has effectively replaced web institutions like forums — and arguably, the lack of permanence is the only thing keeping it from supplanting other popular online communities such as Reddit. As of this writing, Reddit is estimated to have somewhere around 116 million daily active users compared to Discord's 90 million. Even taking into account that many Reddit users browse without logging in, the two platforms are nearly neck and neck. Added discoverability for Discord will undoubtedly help push the platform to more people who might not otherwise log into a server.

highlights.title: 3 Questions: Why infrastructure is entering a defining era
highlights.summary: Professor Ali Jadbabaie describes how AI, digital transformation, climate change, and complex geopolitics are forcing engineers and policymakers to rethink how infrastructure is designed, built, and managed.
body: For centuries, infrastructure has evolved alongside technology. New materials and engineering techniques enabled taller buildings, longer bridges, and larger cities. Computing and digital technologies later transformed how infrastructure was designed, monitored, and operated.

Now, the pace of change is accelerating, and challenges are arriving simultaneously. Climate change is increasing pressure on water, energy, and other resources. Artificial intelligence is beginning to transform engineering and design, and its energy needs, along with aging grid infrastructure, is creating significant challenges, as well as new opportunities. In addition, geopolitical complexity is exposing vulnerabilities in global supply chains, and demand for infrastructure is rising, particularly in the developing world.
The result is a fundamental challenge: How can the world build the infrastructure it needs without simply repeating the extractive, carbon- and resource-intensive model of the 20th century?

highlights.title: "This company has been driven into a wall for years" - Life is Strange studio Don't Nod faces unrest while teetering on insolvency
highlights.summary: There's deep unrest at French studio Don't Nod - creator of Life is Strange, Remember Me, Vampyr, Banishers: New Eden, and most recently Aphelion - as it scrambles to restructure itself and guard against insolvency.
body: Indeed, an impassioned account of proceedings on French union Le Syndicat des Travailleureuses du Jeu Vidéo's website ( via Rock, Paper, Shotgun ) reveals Don't Nod has entered safeguard proceedings - a kind of last-ditch restructuring effort to stave off insolvency. It also reports that even though redundancies are being made,Don't Nod intends to finish making the in-development game codenamed P14, albeit relying more on outsourced development rather than its cut-down in-house team.

The report, which claims knowledge of a memo sent by Don't Nod CEO Oskar Guilbert, and of the goings-on of the Don't Nod employee representatives - the CSE - doubts whether Don't Nod will be able to finish the game. Apparently all of the studio's character artists, concept artists, most of its environment artists, most of its sound designers, game designers, level designers, programmers, producers, testers, and dev-ops have been let go.

"To compensate for this massacre and keep on running with production on a game that, to this day, didn't cut down on its scope and is keeping around a hundred persons busy, management is betting it all on outsourcing," the report says.

highlights.title: xAI is buying out homeowners who promise not to sue over data center noise
highlights.summary: A subsidiary of Elon Musk's xAI is offering to buy up homes in a Mississippi neighborhood, as long as residents don't join a lawsuit targeting the company's nearby data center and power plant, according to a report from The Guardian.
body: xAI and its subsidiary MZX are reportedly offering to buy hundreds of homes around Southaven, Mississippi.

MZX denies all of the allegations against it. However, because MZX also requires property for its business purposes, MZX, through its real estate broker, is offering to purchase real estate in Southaven in exchange for, among other things, a release of all claims related to the lawsuit. If you decide to accept MZX’s offer, MZX will ask you to sign a real estate contract under which you will agree to execute a separate release agreement at the closing of the real estate transaction.

Importantly, by executing the Release Agreement, you will be releasing possible claims you might have related to the Southaven Plant, including any claims you may have in connection with the Haley action. body: In an interview with L'Officiel (via Slash Film ), Dornan candidly said, "I've been asked to play a super-iconic role, and I'll do my best. But for me, Aragorn will always be just Viggo." Mortensen played Aragorn throughout Peter Jackson's The Lord of the Rings film trilogy. Dornan added, "I feel honored to try to recapture at least some of the energy he originally brought to the character." As for how he'll approach the character in the shadow of what came before, the newcomer said, "There’s no part of me that’s trying to outdo him.”

Dornan will be in a unique position amongst the cast, as other iconic Lord of the Rings characters will be reprised by actors from the original films. This includes Elijah Wood and Ian McKellen as Frodo Baggins and Gandalf the Grey, respectively. Director Andy Serkis, who will once again portray Gollum, has revealed the film will use some digital de-aging technology for returning cast members, so the choice to recast Aragorn is an interesting one.

body: If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

There’s the fight in Taylor over plans to build a data center at a site that’s supposed to be a park. Temple, around 40 miles away, is another sore spot, Bledsoe says. The mayor and City Council members there face recall attempts over data center developments. And some 30 miles outside of Austin, San Marcos became the first city in all of Texas to ban data centers.

If there’s one thing a broad range of voters can agree on this election season, it’s that they hate data centers and are unhappy with the status quo. highlights.title: Vampir Is a Dark, Brutal MMORPG Focused on Bloody Violence
highlights.summary: The MMORPG genre has been woefully lacking in vampire representation, but into that void steps Netmarble’s Vampir. It first launched in South Korea in 2025 before recently expanding to the West, and it’s now available in the U.S. on PC, iOS, and Android.
body: This is a game that really leans into the full vampire experience. It’s defined by blood, horror, and sexuality with brutal combat in a dark fantasy setting. From the start of the game, you’ll be treated to some gruesome scenes that set the tone of the world, and that tone carries into gameplay. There are five character classes to choose from, and they’re all aggressive damage dealers that can use vampires’ signature blood-draining abilities to restore HP and gain temporary combat buffs.

All the classes dish out death in stylish fashion, but the way they do it is very different. Carnage can use a variety of firearms with rapid-fire attacks. Bloodstained is a berserker with added durability that can channel its bloodlust into a powerful sword. Viper uses poisons, curses, and summoned creatures to deal AoE damage and control the battlefield. Grim Reaper is a stealth assassin that uses teleportation and a scythe to land critical strikes. And Akasha is a melee class that specializes in pursuing enemies.
points: The MMORPG genre has been woefully lacking in vampire representation, but into that void steps Netmarble’s Vampir.

highlights.title: The Inside Story of Why Apple Finally Brought a Touch Display to the Mac
highlights.summary: An exclusive early look at Apple’s new touchscreen MacBook Pro—the computer Apple said would never happen.
body: It’s a bright day in Cupertino. Apple’s new CEO strolls to an outdoor seating area within the company’s otherworldly ring-shaped headquarters and pulls up a chair. An employee notes the angle and asks if he minds the sun. John Ternus doesn’t mind at all.

Nearly two months into his tenure, he’s been busy. While the tech world buzzes about AI agents and the upcoming IPO of a company reporting spectacular losses, Ternus’ leadership of a ridiculously profitable firm has so far been defined by a sequence of significant launches—the long-awaited foldable iPhone, a household device that can control digital appliances, new Mac Minis, and AirPods. Intentionally or not, all that activity sends a message that, even as AI dominates the public imagination, hardware products still rule.

Ternus doesn’t endorse that take, but he doesn’t object when I suggest it. “We’ve been working on these products for quite some time,” he says. “It feels like everyone here is just kind of riding high right now, enjoying it.”
I ask if Apple is about to break a long-imposed taboo and introduce a Macintosh with a touch screen.
